- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +5% above immediate prior peak.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overbought overreaction.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment oscillating 0.3–0.6), model often fails to revert quickly; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average within 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is falling, model underestimates drop; add 1–3% downward buffer to avoid “sentiment lag” bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to reflect it; apply 2–4% downward adjustment to avoid “lagged optimism” effect.
